experiments.verification_evidence: STATIC_AUDIT. Recomputation: macro R@10 = (49.99+56.62+59.51)/3 = 55.373333 -> 55.37 at 2dp, but the table PRINTS 55.38 (delta +0.0067). macro R@50 = (72.38+74.68+78.53)/3 = 75.196667 -> 75.20 = printed. Mean check both ways: (printed 55.38 + printed 75.20)/2 = 65.29 = printed AVG.; (unrounded macros 55.373333 + 75.196667)/2 = 65.285 -> 65.29 (ROUND_HALF_UP) = printed AVG. So the printed Mean equals (Average R@10 + Average R@50)/2, but the printed Average R@10 is 0.01 higher than the 2dp macro of its own printed categories. Protocol caveat: the paper never states the gallery construction or reference policy; the pinned evaluator defaults to split='original-split' (workbench/third_party/HABIT/datasets.py:28), which enumerates the whole validation image list (datasets.py:205-211), and masks the reference before ranking (test.py:151 sets sims[i, index(source_img_id)] = -10e10, ranking at test.py:154/168), which is what the workbench protocol id fashioniq_full_gallery_ref_excluded encodes. This is the best-supported reading, not something the paper establishes.
experiments.verification_method: Four independent routes agreeing digit-for-digit: (1) arXiv HTML table (machine-readable); (2) `pdftotext -layout -f 5 -l 5 habit.pdf` -> 'HABIT (Ours) 49.99 72.38 56.62 74.68 59.51 78.53 55.38 75.20 65.29'; (3) rendered PDF page 5 image (`pdftoppm -r 150 -f 5 -l 5`) read visually, same values; (4) author-rendered workbench/third_party/HABIT/assets/results-fiq.png, same values. Arithmetic recomputed with Python Decimal ROUND_HALF_UP.
